title: Rank of a valuation on a prime field
statement: Let $F$ be a prime field, i.e. a field isomorphic to $\mathbf Q$ or to $\mathbf F_p$ for a prime $p$ [def-weil-field], and let $A$ be a valuation ring of $F$, i.e. a subring $A\subseteq F$ such that for every $a\in F^\times$ at least one of $a,a^{-1}$ lies in $A$; write $A^\times$ for its unit group. Put $\Gamma_F=F^\times/A^\times$ and $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma_F)=\dim_{\mathbf Q}(\Gamma_F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q)$. Then $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma_F)\le 1$.

source.place: §2.1, the valuation-theoretic discussion preceding Lemma 2.1.2; the prime-field valuation has rank at most one. The local document copy is unavailable.

proof.text: Assume first that $F\cong\mathbf F_p$. Every nonzero element $x$ then satisfies $x^{p-1}=1$. The valuation-ring alternative puts either $x$ or $x^{-1}$ in $A$. In the second case $x=(x^{-1})^{p-2}$ (with the case $p=2$ giving $x=1$), so in either case $x\in A$. Hence $A=F$, every nonzero element is a unit, $\Gamma_F$ is trivial, and $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma_F)=0$.

source.place: §2.1, proof of Corollary 2.1.3(i); the finite-field calculation is written out here because the local copy is unavailable

proof.text:
Now assume $F\cong\mathbf Q$. Since $A$ is a subring, it contains $\mathbf Z$. Let $\mathfrak m\subseteq A$ be the set of $a\in A$ such that $a=0$ or $a^{-1}
otin A$, i.e. the non-invertible elements of $A$. (i) $\mathfrak m$ is closed under multiplication by $A$: if $b\in A$, $s\in\mathfrak m$ and $bs
e0$ had $(bs)^{-1}\in A$, then $s^{-1}=b(bs)^{-1}\in A$, contradicting $s\in\mathfrak m$. (ii) $\mathfrak m$ is closed under addition: let $s,t\in\mathfrak m$; if one of them is $0$ there is nothing to prove, so let both be nonzero. The valuation alternative applied to $s/t$ gives $s=tc$ or $t=sc$ with $c\in A$. In the first case $s+t=t(1+c)$; if $s+t
e0$ and $(s+t)^{-1}\in A$, then $t^{-1}=(1+c)(s+t)^{-1}\in A$, a contradiction; so $s+t\in\mathfrak m$ (this includes $s+t=0$). The second case is symmetric. (iii) $1
otin\mathfrak m$. Now if two distinct rational primes $r$ and $s$ were in $\mathfrak m$, choose $u,v\in\mathbf Z\subseteq A$ with $ur+vs=1$ (Bezout, as $\gcd(r,s)=1$); by (i) $ur,vs\in\mathfrak m$, so by (ii) $1\in\mathfrak m$, contradicting (iii). Thus at most one rational prime is a non-invertible element of $A$; every other rational prime $p$ lies in $\mathbf Z\subseteq A$ with $p^{-1}\in A$, i.e. is a unit of $A$.

source.place: §2.1, proof of Corollary 2.1.3(i); the valuation-ring argument for Q is expanded here because the local copy is unavailable

proof.text: If no rational prime is non-invertible in $A$, every rational prime and its inverse are units, so every element of $\mathbf Q^\times$ is a unit and $\Gamma_F$ is trivial. Otherwise let $r$ be the unique rational prime in $\mathfrak m$. Every other prime is a unit, and unique factorization writes each $x\in\mathbf Q^\times$ as a sign times a finite product of integral powers of rational primes; modulo $A^\times$ its class is therefore an integral power of the class of $r$. Thus $\Gamma_F$ is generated by one element, so $\Gamma_F\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ has $\mathbf Q$-dimension at most one. This proves $\operatorname{rrk}(\Gamma_F)\le1$ in both cases.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N5-136a3bad0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The statement is self-contained (valuation ring defined inline, stmt_dep def-weil-field) and true. I tested it on A=F (rank 0), on Z_(p) (Gamma=Z, rank 1) and on F_2 (A=F forced). The parent lem-trf-abhyankar-finite-type-field-height (step 3) applies it to A cap F and uses exactly the bound rrk<=1. Step 1 (F_p): since x^{p-1}=1, x=(x^{-1})^{p-2}, so A=F; the p=2 case also holds. Step 3: Gamma is cyclic by unique factorization, given that at most one prime is non-invertible. Steps 1 and 3 are correct and elementary. One repairable fault, in step 2: it defined a nonunit as a nonzero non-invertible element and then claimed a sum of nonunits is a nonunit. That is false for r+(-r)=0, and the phrase 'zero causes no issue' did not fix it. The inverse computations and the Bezout argument themselves are correct. I rewrote step 2 using m={a in A: a=0 or a^{-1} not in A}, proving closure under A-multiples and under addition and that 1 is not in m, and aligned step 3's wording. The fix file is fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/lem-trf-prime-field-valuation-rank.json; only the proof texts changed. There are no new nodes, no citations and no tool_uses, so there is no route issue on sk-i-curve-zero.
